interest: This file is particularly valuable for historians studying Japan's pre-World War II withdrawal from international conservation agreements and its drive toward resource self-sufficiency. It captures Japan's intention to exploit fur seal herds in the Arctic and North Pacific immediately upon the expiration of the 1911 Fur Seal Treaty in October 1941, detailing commercial exploitation plans by the Kurile Islands Development Company for meat, blubber oil, and pharmaceutical hormones. In addition, the file illustrates internal State Department linguistic and legal procedures across the Treaty Division, Translating Bureau, and Division of Far Eastern Affairs as officers scrutinized Japanese maritime ordinances and factory-ship processing limits, while demonstrating how related marine mammal records (sealing and whaling) occasionally intersected in decimal filings.
overview: Decimal file 894.627 covers State Department records between February 1939 and September 1944 relating to Japanese marine mammal exploitation, primarily fur seal hunting and related regulatory translation matters. The file includes a March 1941 voluntary report from the American Embassy in Tokyo describing Japan's plans to resume large-scale commercial fur seal hunting in the Arctic and North Pacific following the termination of the 1911 Four-Power Fur Seal Convention, as well as a 1944 cross-reference sheet noting Tokyo radio broadcasts regarding seal catches. It also contains an internal State Department memorandum exchange from February and March 1939 between the Treaty Division, the Translating Bureau, and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding the precise translation of Japanese whaling regulations governing factory ship catch limits and 36-hour processing windows from a Yokohama consular report.

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese plans to engage in extensive commercial fur seal hunting following the expiration of the four-power seal protection treaty in October 1941.
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This voluntary report prepared by American Vice Consul Donald W. Lamm and approved by Commercial Attaché Frank S. Williams outlines Japanese intentions to resume large-scale pelagic fur seal hunting after the 1911 four-power convention expires on October 22, 1941. Citing an article in the Hochi Shimbun and statements by S. Yokota, president of the Kurile Islands Development Company, the report projects annual catches of up to 600,000 seals from Arctic herds estimated at 6,000,000. It details expected commercial uses of the animals, including furs, meat for food in northeastern Japan, oil from blubber, and hormone medicines produced from entrails.
subfiles.title: Voluntary Report No. 159: Japanese to Engage in Fur Seal Hunting

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note for a State Department letter to the Interior Department concerning Tokyo radio reports on Japanese seal catches.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes a September 4, 1944 letter sent to the Department of the Interior, originally filed under decimal 711.417/9-444. The underlying communication comments on Tokyo radio broadcasts regarding the catch of fur seals by the Japanese. It links wartime Japanese exploitation of seal resources back to the central fur seal subject classification.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Comments on Tokyo Radio Reports on Catch of Seals

subfiles.about: Provides an authoritative Far Eastern Affairs translation and correction for a Japanese whaling regulation regarding factory ship processing capacity.
subfiles.from: Leo D. Sturgeon, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Drafted by Leo D. Sturgeon in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, this memorandum responds to the Translating Bureau's request to verify Part II of a Yokohama Consulate report on whaling dated December 2, 1938. Sturgeon confirms that the consulate's English translation is substantially accurate except for Section 41, subsection (c). He supplies Far Eastern Affairs' corrected translation requiring mother ship operators to ensure whales are not captured beyond the capacity to process them within 36 hours.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Translation of Yokohama Consulate Whaling Report

subfiles.about: Transmits a Treaty Division file to Far Eastern Affairs requesting assistance in translating a page of Japanese text.
subfiles.summary: This inter-office memorandum from the Translating Bureau forwards a Treaty Division file to Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. The bureau requests Far Eastern Affairs' expertise to translate a Japanese-language page attached to the file. It asks that the documents be returned to the Translating Bureau as soon as convenient.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Requesting Japanese Translation Assistance
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Requests the Translating Bureau to check the translation in Part II of a consular despatch against its Japanese text.
subfiles.summary: This brief internal memorandum from the Treaty Division asks Mr. Christie of the Translating Bureau to examine Part II of a consular despatch on whaling. The recipient is asked to check the English translation against the original Japanese text located on the final page of the file. This request initiated the inter-divisional review that resulted in Far Eastern Affairs' revised translation of maritime catch restrictions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Requesting Verification of Japanese Whaling Despatch Translation

subfiles.about: Directs Treaty Division staff to specific pages and sections of a report concerning Japanese Ordinance No. 22 of June 8, 1938.
subfiles.summary: This internal routing slip from the Division of Communications and Records is addressed to Miss Freeman in the Treaty Division at the Winder Building. It directs the reader to Part II, Page 4 of a report under the heading 'Government Control' for Japanese Ordinance No. 22 of June 8, 1938. The note serves as a reference guide for navigating regulatory documentation on marine industries.
subfiles.title: Routing Note to Miss Freeman Concerning Japanese Ordinance No. 22
